Radomyshl Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Zhytomyrska oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. A Jewish barber in Radomyshl was tried on ritual murder charges and acquitted in 1839. The community reached 7,502 people (69 percent of the town) by 1897, supporting an extensive religious and educational infrastructure. During the pogroms of the Civil War era, the congregation's spiritual leader, Rabbi Avrom Yehoshua Heschel Twerski, was among the hundreds killed. An ohel was built over the Twerski burials in this cemetery in the early 21st century, and the cemetery's fence was renovated in 2019.
